title.en: Static and instance members; scope of variables

hook.en: Every student has a roll number of their own, but the school name is shared by all. Java marks shared members static; everything else belongs to each object.

objectives.en: Distinguish class (static) variables from instance variables
Call static and instance methods correctly
State the scope and lifetime of local, instance and class variables

narration.en: Every student has a roll number of their own, but the school name is shared by all. Java marks shared members static; everything else belongs to each object.

body.en: An instance variable belongs to an object: each object has its own copy, created with the object. A static (class) variable belongs to the class: there is exactly one copy, shared by all objects, created when the class is loaded. Static methods are called on the class name (Math.sqrt) and can use only static members directly; instance methods are called on an object (s1.display()) and can use both.

points.en: Static: one copy per class, shared
Static methods: no this, only static members directly

body.en: The scope of a variable is the part of the program where it can be used. A local variable (declared inside a method or block, including parameters and loop variables) is visible only from its declaration to the end of that block and exists only while the block runs. An instance variable is visible in all instance methods of the class and lives as long as its object. A class variable is visible throughout the class and lives as long as the class is loaded. A local variable with the same name as a field hides (shadows) the field.

problem.en: Find the output: class Demo { static int s = 0; int n = 0; Demo() { s++; n++; } } … Demo p = new Demo(); Demo q = new Demo(); System.out.println(p.s + " " + p.n + " " + q.s + " " + q.n);

steps.en: Each constructor call adds 1 to the shared s and 1 to its own n.
After two objects: s = 2 (shared); p.n = 1; q.n = 1.
